subtle.$description: Byte-identical to surface-raised (2026-07-27 review) — a hover fill (subtle) on a control inside an elevated card (surface-raised) is visually invisible as a result. Tried moving to gray.700 to fix that, but it fails AA for the real text.secondary-on-bg.subtle pairing (Tag/Badge subtleNeutral): 4.00:1, needs 4.5:1. gray.600 is worse (2.73:1). No primitive step exists between 800 and 900 to resolve the surface-raised collision without breaking contrast, so this stays at gray.800 — the collision is a real but lower-priority design nit, not a WCAG failure, and accessibility takes priority per CLAUDE.md.

brand-hover.$description: Darker than brand (breaks the usual 'dark mode lightens on hover' direction, same deviation already established for bg.danger-hover below) — purple.400 only gives white text 3.41:1, failing AA; purple.600 gives 7.37:1 (verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). purple.300 (lighter still) would only make it worse (2.43:1).

danger-hover.$description: Lighter than danger, restoring the usual dark-mode 'brighten on hover' direction (Phase 4 OKLCH regen, 2026-07-18) now that text.on-danger is gray.950 in dark mode: gray.950 on red.400 = 7.44:1. The earlier fix used red.600 (darker) specifically because it paired with white text (3.24:1 on red.400 failed then) — that constraint no longer applies now that on-danger is theme-specific.

warning-hover.$description: Lighter than warning, restoring the usual dark-mode 'brighten on hover' direction (2026-07-27), mirroring bg.danger-hover: gray.950 text.on-warning on amber.400 = 7.76:1, passes AA.

success-hover.$description: Lighter than success, restoring the usual dark-mode 'brighten on hover' direction (2026-07-27), mirroring bg.danger-hover: gray.950 text.on-success on green.400 = 8.23:1, passes AA.

info-hover.$description: Lighter than info, restoring the usual dark-mode 'brighten on hover' direction (2026-07-27), mirroring bg.danger-hover: gray.950 text.on-info on blue.400 = 7.83:1, passes AA.

neutral.$description: Fifth status-tone fill, for neutral/offline-style indicators (e.g. Avatar's offline status dot). gray.500 on bg.surface: 3.25:1 light / 4.34:1 dark, both pass WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1) — re-verified 2026-07-18 (Phase 4, OKLCH regen), shared across all 4 themes since gray.500 uniquely satisfies both.

neutral-strong.$description: Solid neutral fill for hosting text (Badge's solid variant, neutral tone) — bg.neutral (gray.500) is only verified for the 3:1 non-text case. gray.600 with white text gives 4.70:1, passing everywhere — shared across all 4 themes (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

overlay.$description: Dimming scrim behind Dialog/Drawer/overlays (Backdrop atom). No text sits directly on it, so it isn't a WCAG contrast pairing — opacity is applied separately, compositionally, via the opacity.* scale rather than baked into this token, matching how color and opacity stay separate token categories everywhere else. Shared across all 4 themes since dimming what's behind isn't a brand-dependent decision.

tertiary.$description: gray.500 fails AA (needs 4.5:1) for this token's literal-text uses (Text color="tertiary", Divider label, Input placeholder). gray.400 gives 6.08:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen), still more muted than text.secondary (gray.300).

on-danger.$description: Text on a solid bg.danger fill. Post-OKLCH-regen (Phase 4, 2026-07-18): dark-theme bg.danger is red.500, where white only gives 3.48:1. gray.950 gives 5.22:1 (and 7.44:1 against danger-hover's red.400) — this token is now theme-specific; light themes keep white (5.10:1 against red.600).

on-info.$description: Text on a solid bg.info fill (Badge solid variant). Post-OKLCH-regen (Phase 4, 2026-07-18): dark-theme bg.info is blue.500, where white only gives 3.26:1. gray.950 gives 5.56:1 — this token is now theme-specific; light themes keep white (4.71:1 against blue.600).

on-success.$description: Text on a solid bg.success fill (Badge solid variant). Dark-theme bg.success is green.500: white fails (3.07:1), gray.950 passes at 5.91:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Light themes now use white instead — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json.

on-warning.$description: Text on a solid bg.warning fill (Badge solid variant). Dark-theme bg.warning is amber.500: white fails (3.31:1), gray.950 passes at 5.49:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Light themes now use white instead — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json.

on-neutral.$description: Text on a solid bg.neutral-strong fill (Badge solid variant). White on gray.600 = 4.70:1, passes everywhere — shared across all 4 themes (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

link.$description: purple.400 on bg.surface (gray.900) is 4.13:1, failing AA after the Phase 4 OKLCH regen. purple.300 gives 5.80:1 (verified 2026-07-18).

brand.$description: Accent text drawn from the brand color (2026-07-27) — for emphasis/labels, not links (see text.link). Reuses the same resolved value as text.link: purple.600 (the literal brand anchor) on gray.900 is only 1.92:1, badly failing AA — purple.300 gives 5.80:1.

Brand-accent border, decorative-only (2026-07-27, revised from purple.400). Literal brand.100 in every theme — this token is for decorative UI accents, not a border that identifies a component/state boundary (WCAG 1.4.11 doesn't apply the same way here; border.focus/border.danger remain contrast-verified since those ARE state-identifying). purple.100 on gray.900 is 12.38:1, very high contrast in dark mode even though light mode is intentionally low.
